newsitem.title: USA: Wet weather delays Kansas harvest, wheat seeding.
newsitem.headline: Wet weather delays Kansas harvest, wheat seeding.

text.p: Rains across much of Kansas prevented farmers from completing much fieldwork during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
Twenty percent of Kansas wheat acreage was seeded, lagging 28 percent last year and the 46-percent average.
Harvest of fall crops made little progress due to rain. Twenty percent of the state's corn was harvested, versus 11 last year and the average of 32 percent.
Corn condition was rated 86 percent good to excellent, 12 fair and two poor to very poor.
Sorghum condition was rated 86 percent good to excellent, 12 percent fair and two percent poor. Nine percent of sorghum was harvested, versus two last year and the average of 12.
Soybeans were rated 83 percent good to excellent, 16 fair and one percent poor. Five percent of the crop was harvested, versus two percent last year and the average of 14 percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated 55 percent adequate and 45 percent surplus.
Pasture condition was rated 78 percent good to excellent, 18 percent fair and four percent poor.
